text:
maya: quick RFC follow-up on the incremental-patch/operator handshake idea. sketched a flow in the doc but want concrete answers for two UX/safety gaps before we fold into the RFC: how do we detect "incomplete activation" across reboots, and what should the operator do on a mid-apply power failure? short thread please.

jon: +1. my proposal: model the apply as a 5-state finite state machine: TRANSFER -> VERIFY -> STAGE -> ACTIVATE -> FINALIZE. write idempotent marker files after each state transition so restart can resume from last committed state.

maya: simple enough. what form do the markers take? files on disk? k8s CR status? both?

jon: markers: on-node: /var/lib/redwood/patch-state.json (signed by agent key). also push minimal boolean state into the Operator CR status so control-plane can show progress without heavy logs.

li: we need the marker to include a resume token (opaque blob) that encodes which blob ranges were applied. token must be sealed to cluster KMS so offline attackers can't forge progress.

anita: caution: for air-gapped islands we can't rely on cluster KMS being reachable for unseal during resume. agent must support local sealed storage (HSM/KMS plugin) or allow operator to provide the unseal key via admin workflow.

derek: from SRE side: automatic rollback rule: if STATE==STAGE for >10m and agent process restarts repeatedly (>=3 restarts within 5m), mark node unhealthy and initiate rollback-to-previous-image. avoid leaving nodes partially active.

maya: ok rollback window seems fine. what about partial-blob application (we applied range 0..X of blob B)? resume needs to be incrementally aware.

jon: we use chunked blobs and per-chunk hash verification. marker contains last-applied-chunk-index per blob. on resume we verify chain continuity: next chunk must start at last_index+1. if mismatch, fail safe (halt and require manual reconciliation).

anita: ops-loop: operator should surface a dry-run reconcile that simulates resume checks: `redwoodctl operator inspect-resume --node N --token <token>` returns a minimal plan. that helps admin decide manual steps when mismatch occurs.

li: signing: manifest and each delta must be signed by publisher key. agent verifies signature chain before WRITE. for KMS-escrow: recommend storing a per-cluster escrow envelope that unwraps with customer KMS, not our keys. for airgap installs, provide an offline unseal tool that takes a signed admin approval into the operator.

derek: we also need good observability: events for TRANSFER/VERIFY/STAGE/ACTIVATE/FINALIZE and metrics for time-in-state. add a tracing tag `upgrade.session_id` so we can correlate logs across nodes.

maya: UX question: operator console--should we allow "force-complete" from web UI or restrict to CLI+two-admin-signatures?

jon: strongly prefer CLI + two-admin-signatures for force ops. UI can show a button but it should trigger a CLI workflow requiring signatures.

anita: real-world note: physical power-loss on remote sites is common. operator should support a configurable "grace window" (default 15m) where nodes can auto-retry resume X times before escalation. on escalation, send a single-line playbook: "operator run reconcile --node N --manual true".

li: fallback modes: (1) normal resume using sealed token, (2) offline-admin-unseal where admin provides an unwrap blob and a timestamped justification signed by 2 admins, (3) last-resort: full-image-swap rollback. document these as ordered fallbacks.

ops-bot: [agent] apply-session 0x9f3a started on node r-node-7 (session_id=0x9f3a)

derek: can we standardize the CLI resume token format now? base64 of protobuf {session_id, last_chunk_map, sign, timestamp} encrypted with KMS. keeps token small and machine parseable.

maya: agreed. last Q: operator API for downstream apps that depend on activation (eg routing layer) — should Operator set Kubernetes readiness only after FINALIZE or after ACTIVATE?

jon: set readiness after ACTIVATE but before FINALIZE so routing can begin traffic while finalization (non-traffic-impacting steps like attic cleanup) completes. but include a `traffic_allowed` boolean in CR so controllers know whether to gradually send traffic.

anita: one more: we should mirror the marker blobs to a pull-cache (local registry) during TRANSFER so resume is possible even if original media is lost. cache retention policy pluggable.

maya: great thread. I'll capture these decisions as bullets in the RFC follow-up: - FSM + on-disk + CR status markers - resume token sealed to KMS with offline-unseal fallback - per-chunk resume index + fail-safe on mismatch - default rollback and escalation windows - CLI two-admin signature for force ops - readiness after ACTIVATE + traffic flag - local pull-cache optional. I'll ping for reviews once I update the RFC.

jon: thanks. I'll draft the marker JSON schema and sample CLI snippets.

li: I'll add the KMS/escrow diagrams and offline-unseal tool UX.

anita: I'll prototype the local cache and retention knobs.

derek: I'll add the SLO/alerting playbook and runbook entries.

maya: thanks all. syncing later today. :thumbsup:
